newsitem.title: INDIA: India must target higher groundnut exports-trade.
newsitem.headline: India must target higher groundnut exports-trade.

text.p: India should target higher groundnut exports of 105,000 tonnes in 1996/97 (April-March) representing a total value of 2.5 billion rupees, a leading oil trade association said on Friday.
India exported an estimated 90,000 tonnes of groundnuts in 1995/96 totalling 2.07 billion rupees, Mulraj Tanna, chairman of Indian Oil & Produce Exporters Association told an annual meeting.
Tanna said he expected groundnut prices to be "steady to higher" in the coming months.

"While the world demand for peanuts is growing at about five percent per annum, India's exports have got to grow faster so as to garner a decent market share commensurate with our share in the world peanut production," Tanna said.
He said India exported an estimated 15,000 tonnes of groundnuts totalling 350 million rupees during April-August 1996.
He said sesame seed exports reached a high of 70,000 tonnes valued at 2.1 billion rupees during 1995/96 compared to 55,000 tonnes worth 1.35 billion rupees in the previous year.
India was consolidating its position in markets including Egypt and Israel and was targetting new markets like Guatemala.
"We have also re-established our product, after a gap of three years, in the highly quality conscious American markets," Tanna said.
"Our aim should now be to reach 100,000 tonnes export of sesame seed, representing 20 percent of world trade, in the next two or three seasons," he said.
